newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki heartened by U.S. data, rises 1.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki heartened by U.S. data, rises 1.3 pct.

text.p: Shares dashed ahead late in the session on Friday bringing the HEX index up 1.32 percent to close at 2,972.49 after U.S. payrolls data soothed interest rate hike jitters overseas and at home, brokers said.
"The (U.S.) figures were good, and forestry shares took off," one broker said.
The late burst of activity pushed volume up to a sound 540 million markka for the day, over half of it in Nokia.
"If the U.S. stock market continues to rise today, it will give us a good boost for Monday," another broker said.
Forestry group Enso stood out, putting on 1.50 markka to end at 44.50 in sturdy 17 million markka volume, while UPM-Kymmene rose 2.00 markka to end at 121.00 in 37 million markka trade.
While forestries outperformed, Nokia closed 4.10 markka higher at 328.50, but off an intraday high of 330.50.
"With Nokia, if the buying lets up just for a moment, then the price starts to trickle," one broker said.
Rautaruukki continued to trade well above its offering price of 42.00 markka per share, rising 1.50 to 47.10 markka in good 15 million markka volume.
Outokumpu got in on the goodwill towards metal shares and rose 0.20 markka to 99.20 after touching 100.00
PK Cables ended up 4.00 markka at a life-high 78.00 markka. Brokers said it was tracking Nokia higher.

Huhtamaki ailed, falling 5.50 markka to 220.00. Brokers said the share has been falling recently on foreign selling, and unflattering foreign recommendations, including a report on Friday that Merrill Lynch was starting it at "reduce."
